If you have limited space, look into square foot gardening. You don't have to buy the book. Here are the basics. Use boards, hardy planking, or concrete to make 3' x 3' squares around a foot deep. You can put weed blocking cloth under them and chicken wire to keep out moles if you wish. Fill the square boxes with a mix of 1/3 compost, 1/3 peat moss, and 1/3 vermiculite, all by volume. The compost needs to be a mix of whatever kinds you can get, including cow, chicken, mushroom, etc. The mix will always stay loose. The small size of the boxes means you never have to step in them and compress the mix.

Divide each box into 9 little squares. You will plant seeds or plants in each little square at recommended distances, but not in a row but all over the square. This gives you a lot of plants in a small area. You will be amazed at how much you can grow in a small area. The dense planting also keeps the weeds down. You never have to add fertilizer. Each year just compost the plants you pull out, and then add that back into the boxes. If that isn't enough to finish filling the boxes, buy a little more compost to mix in.

You can grow all the vegetables you can eat in a small yard, as long as you aren't completely in the shade. You can also plant more veggies as soon as some are harvested right through your growing season.
